questions.prompt: Roll two fair dice. Given that the sum is 7, what is the probability that the first die shows 2?
questions.model_answer: 1/6 — there are 6 outcomes with sum 7, and only (2,5) fits.
questions.explanation: Restrict the sample space to the 6 outcomes whose sum is 7. 1/36 forgets to restrict; 2/7 and 1/3 don't come from a correct count.

questions.prompt: A disease affects 2% of people, the test's sensitivity is 90%, and its false-positive rate is 10%. Roughly what is P(sick | positive)?
questions.explanation: By Bayes, the denominator also includes the false positives among healthy people. 90% confuses P(+|sick) with P(sick|+).

questions.prompt: A and B are disjoint events with P(A)=0.3 and P(B)=0.4. Which is true?
questions.explanation: Disjointness with positive probabilities implies dependence — if A happened, B certainly didn't.

questions.prompt: In your own words, explain why linearity of expectation is useful even when the variables are dependent, and give an example.
questions.model_answer: E[X+Y]=E[X]+E[Y] follows from the linearity of the sum and doesn't require independence; for example, counting the fixed points of a permutation as a sum of dependent indicators gives an expectation of 1.
questions.explanation: The key point is that you don't need the joint distribution.
